_meta.threadlinqs/catalog_note: Served from the public catalog, not your authenticated tool list. Check THREADLINQS_API_KEY.

description: Flagship one-call hunting dossier for a threat: threat detail + similar threats + simulations + infrastructure pivots, composed server-side. Best single tool to scope a hunt around one threat. Every section is bounded so the bundle fits in one response — raise simulation_limit / pivot_limit, or call get_infrastructure_pivots and get_threat directly, when you need the full lists.

pivot_limit.description: Infrastructure pivots to embed, 1-200 (default 25). One threat can carry 150+; get_infrastructure_pivots returns the full set.

shape.description: "v1" (default, unchanged nested envelope) | "canonical" (flat, stably-named, SMALLER — recommended for programmatic consumers) | "both". In canonical: technique ids are a top-level `ttps` array, sectors/regions use ONE spelling, and every array key is ALWAYS an array (never null, never an object). In v1, `similar_threats` and `infrastructure_pivots` are handler envelopes (objects) while `threat.similar_threats` is a flat array — if you are writing a parser, use canonical.

name: get_threat_hunting_bundle

_envelope.description: Shape manifest — announces that shape="canonical" exists.

counts.description: canonical: a denominator for every array key.

infrastructure_pivots.description: v1: handler envelope {threat_id, infrastructure_pivots[], coverage{}} — an OBJECT.

iocs.description: canonical: FLAT array. (In v1 this is an object keyed by category under threat.iocs.)

similar_threats.description: v1: handler envelope {source_threat_id, count, similar[]} — an OBJECT, not an array.

ttps.description: Canonical MITRE technique ids, present in BOTH shapes.

title: Threat Hunting Bundle
